title: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
description: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW updates an existing view's underlying query in place, without needing to DROP it first (and without breaking anything else that references it, as long as the output columns stay compatible). First CREATE VIEW `pricey_products` returning products priced above 30; then, in a second statement, CREATE OR REPLACE the same view so it returns products priced above 40 instead.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
Two statements, same view name both times - the second one just adds OR REPLACE and changes the WHERE threshold from 30 to 40. What the view returns afterward reflects only the SECOND definition.
CREATE VIEW pricey_products AS ... (price > 30); CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pricey_products AS ... (price > 40).
expected_behavior: pricey_products ends up returning name and price for products priced above 40 - the first definition is completely superseded by the second.
solution: CREATE VIEW pricey_products AS SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 30; CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pricey_products AS SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 40;
explanation: Without OR REPLACE, redefining a view means DROP VIEW first - which fails if anything else depends on it. OR REPLACE sidesteps that as long as the new query's output columns are compatible with the old one's.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT name, price FROM pricey_products ORDER BY price DESC
hidden_tests.label: pricey_products reflects only the replaced definition
